questions.q: What problem does Dataverse solve that Castlebridge Logistics kept running into with its shared spreadsheet?
options: Spreadsheets can't be opened on mobile devices
Lack of structured data types, real relationships, and row/column-level security
Spreadsheets cannot be connected to Power Automate at all
Spreadsheets are more expensive to license than Dataverse
questions.explain: The lesson's spreadsheet example (duplicate rows, broken formulas, no real security) illustrates exactly what structured tables, enforced data types, and built-in security solve.

questions.q: In Dataverse terminology, what is a 'row'?
options: A structured entity made up of columns
One record inside a table
A link between two tables
The connector itself inside Power Automate
questions.explain: A row is one record inside a table — for example, one shipment inside Castlebridge's Shipments table.

questions.q: What does a relationship between two Dataverse tables let you do?
options: Merge the two tables into a single table permanently
Reference a row in another table directly, instead of retyping its data
Automatically delete rows in both tables at once
Convert a table into a SharePoint list
questions.explain: A relationship lets one table's row point at a row in another table, so Castlebridge's Shipments table can reference an actual Drivers row instead of a driver's name being retyped by hand.

questions.q: How does Dataverse appear inside Power Automate?
options: As a separate application you must leave Power Automate to use
As a connector, with its own triggers and actions, like any other connector
Only as a manual file import option
It cannot be used inside Power Automate at all
questions.explain: Dataverse shows up in Power Automate as a connector — the same pattern as the Outlook or SharePoint connectors — carrying its own triggers and actions.

questions.q: Which of these correctly matches a Dataverse term to its meaning?
options: Column = one record inside a table
Table = one field on a record
Row = one record inside a table
Row = a structured entity made of tables
questions.explain: A row is one record inside a table; a column is one field on that record; a table is the structured entity that holds both.
